This can lead to orphaned records or data integrity issues if a 'campagne_contacts' entry exists without a corresponding 'contact'. Human review is needed to determine if this column should be made NOT NULL or if the application logic correctly handles null values.
cards.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, COUNT(contact_id) AS non_null_rows, (COUNT(*) - COUNT(contact_id)) AS null_rows, (CAST(COUNT(*) - COUNT(contact_id) AS DECIMAL) / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS null_percentage FROM campagne_contacts;
verification_queries: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, COUNT(contact_id) AS non_null_rows, (COUNT(*) - COUNT(contact_id)) AS null_rows, (CAST(COUNT(*) - COUNT(contact_id) AS DECIMAL) / COUNT(*)) * 100 AS null_percentage FROM campagne_contacts;
rollback_queries: No direct rollback for advisory finding. Manual review and decision required.

cards.title: Remove Duplicate Values and Add Unique Constraint to prm_organization.code
cards.rationale: The 'code' column in 'prm_organization' has 10 duplicate values, violating the uniqueness expectation for columns matching the '*_code' pattern. This fix will remove duplicate rows, keeping one instance, and then add a unique constraint to prevent future duplicates. Data deleted cannot be rolled back.
cards.sql: DELETE FROM prm_organization WHERE ctid NOT IN (SELECT MIN(ctid) FROM prm_organization GROUP BY code); ALTER TABLE prm_organization ADD CONSTRAINT prm_organization_code_unique UNIQUE (code);
verification_queries: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM prm_organization GROUP BY code HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'prm_organization'::regclass AND conname = 'prm_organization_code_unique;
rollback_queries: ALTER TABLE prm_organization DROP CONSTRAINT prm_organization_code_unique;
